insight.title: You Are Imagining the Ancient World in the Wrong Color
insight.subtitle: Why the "classic" look of white marble was actually a historical accident.

sections.text: Every Roman statue you have ever seen was originally painted in loud, garish colors. We imagine a world of white marble, but the ancients actually lived in a landscape of bright, vivid paint.

Over centuries, the colors weathered away, leaving only the bare stone. When Renaissance artists rediscovered these statues, they mistakenly assumed the white marble was a deliberate choice of a pure and clean style.

This error defined how we build today. We constructed our most serious government buildings in plain white because we didn't realize the originals actually looked more like a vibrant, colorful carnival.
We built our world to match a ruin, not a civilization.
